verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा वाक्यं कौरवनन्दनः। हन्त धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यामि दृढे वाङ्मनसी मम॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said Tell me, O grandfather, the marks of future greatness and future degeneration of a person.

verses.sanskrit: तव प्रसादाद्गोविन्द भूतात्मा ह्यसि शाश्वतः। युधिष्ठिरस्तु धर्मात्मा मां धर्माननुपृच्छतु। एवं प्रीतो भविष्यामि धर्मान्वक्ष्यामि चाखिलान्॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Blessings to you, the mind itself indicates the symptoms of one's future prosperity and future fall.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन् राजर्षभे जाते धर्मात्मनि महात्मनि। अहृष्यन् ऋषयः सर्वे स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डव॥३॥
verses.english: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Shree and Shakra. Listen to it, O Yudhishthira.
verses.bhavadeepa: भूतात्मा प्राणिनामन्तरात्माऽसि तेन ममाभिप्रायं वेत्सीति भावः ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेषां दीप्तयशसां कुरूणां धर्मचारिणाम्। यस्य नास्ति समः कश्चित् स मां पृच्छतुं पाण्डवः॥४॥
verses.english: The great and energetic ascetic Narada, whose effulgence is as immeasurable as Brahma itself, with sins all dissipated, capable of seeing through the power of his penances both this and the other world at once, and the equal of the celestial Rishis living in the region of the Creator, roamed at his pleasure through the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: धृतिर्दमो ब्रह्मचर्यं क्षमा धर्मश्च नित्यदा। यस्मिन्नोजश्च स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥५॥
verses.english: One day, rising up early in the morning, he wished to perform his ablutions and for that purpose went to the river Ganga as the issued out of the pass called Dhruva, and plunged into the stream.

verses.sanskrit: सम्बन्धीनतिथीन्भृत्यान् संश्रितांश्चैव यो भृशम्। सम्मानयति सत्कृत्य स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥६॥
verses.english: At that time the thousand-eyed Indra also, the holder of the thunder-bolt, and the destroyer of Shamvara and Paka, came to the very shore where Narada was.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं दानं तपः शौर्यं शान्तिर्दाक्ष्यमसम्भ्रमः। यस्मिन्नेतानि सर्वाणि स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥७॥
verses.english: The Rishi and the god, both of whom had perfectly controlled their minds, finished their ablutions, and having completed their silent recitations, sat together.

verses.sanskrit: यो न कामान्न संरम्भान्न भयान्नार्थकारणात्। कुर्यादधर्मं धर्मात्मा स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥८॥
verses.english: They spent the hour in reciting and listening to the excellent narratives told by the great celestial Rishis describing many good and high deeds. Indeed, with rapt attention the two were engaged in such lively discourse on ancient history.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यनित्यः क्षमानित्यो ज्ञाननित्योऽतिथिप्रियः। यो ददाति सतां नित्यं स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥९॥
verses.english: While sitting there they saw the rising Sun casting his thousand rays right before him. Seeing the full orb, both of them stood up and lauded him.

verses.sanskrit: इज्याध्ययननित्यस्य धर्मे च निरतः सदा। क्षान्तः श्रुतरहस्यश्च स मां पृच्छतु पाण्डवः॥१०॥
verses.english: Just at that time they saw in the sky, in a direction opposite to that of the rising star of day, some luminous object, resplendent as burning fire which seemed to be a second star of day. And they saw, O Bharata, that that luminous object was gradually approaching them both.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेव उवाच। लज्जया परयोपेतो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। अभिशापभयाद्भीतो भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥११॥
verses.english: Riding upon Vishnu's vehicle adorned with Garuda and Surya himself, that object shone forth with matchless splendour and seemed to the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: लोकस्य कदनं कृत्वा लोकनाथो विशाम्पते। अभिशापभयाद्भीतो भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥१२॥
verses.english: The object they beheld was none other than Shree herself, attended by many Apsaras gifted with splendid beauty. Indeed, she looked like a large solar discherself, effulgent like fire.

verses.sanskrit: पूज्यान्मान्यांश्च भक्तांश्च गुरून् सम्बन्धिबान्धवान्। अर्घार्हानिषुभिर्भित्त्वा भवन्तं नोपसर्पति॥१३॥
verses.english: Decorated with ornaments that appeared like veritable stars, she wore a wreath resembling a garland of pearls. Indra saw that goddess called Padma living in the midst of lotuses. light up

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              ब्राह्मणानां यथा धर्मो दानमध्ययनं तपः। क्षत्रियाणां तथा कृष्ण समरे देहपातनम्॥१४॥
verses.english: Getting down from her foremost of cars, that peerless lady began to approach towards the lord of the three worlds and the celestial Rishi Narada.

verses.sanskrit: पितॄन्पितामहान्भ्रातॄन् गुरून्सम्बन्धिबान्धवान्। मिथ्याप्रवृत्तान् यः संख्ये निहन्याद्धर्म एव सः॥१५॥
verses.english: Followed by Narada, Indra also proceeded towards that lady. With joined hands, he offered himself up to her, and versed as he was with all things, he adored her with unsurpassed reverence and sincerity. The adorations over, the king of gods, O king, addressed Shree thus.
verses.bhavadeepa: गोत्रवधजां ग्लानिं धर्मराजस्यापनेष्यन् भीष्म उवाच- ब्राह्मणानामिति ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: समयत्यागिनो लुब्धान् गुरूनपि च केशव। निहन्ति समरे पापान्क्षत्रियो यः स धर्मवित्॥१६॥
verses.english: Shakra said-'O you of sweet smiles, who, indeed, are you and for what have you come here? O you of fair brows, whence do you come and where will you go, O auspicious lady?'

verses.sanskrit: यो लोभान्न समीक्षेत धर्मसेतुं सनातनम्। निहन्ति यस्तं समरे क्षत्रियो वै स धर्मवित्॥१७॥
verses.english: 'In the three worlds full auspiciousness, all creatures, mobile and immobile, try with their whole hearts to gain a companionship with me.

verses.sanskrit: लोहितोदां केशतृणां गजशैलां ध्वजद्रुमाम्। महीं करोति युद्धेषु क्षत्रियो यः स धर्मवित्॥१८॥
verses.english: I am that Padma, that Shree adorned with lotuses, who originated from the lotus that blooms at the touch of the rays of the Sun-god, for the prosperity of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: आहूतेन रणे नित्यं योद्धव्यं क्षत्रबन्धुना। धर्म्यं स्वर्ग्यं च लोक्यं च युद्धं हि मनुरब्रवीत्॥१९॥
verses.english: I am called Lakshmi, Bhuti, and Sree, O killer of Vala! I am Faith, I am Intelligence, I am Affluence, I am Victory, and I am Immutability.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तस्तु भीष्मेण धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। विनीतवदुपागम्य तस्थौ संदर्शनेऽग्रतः॥२०॥
verses.english: I am Patience. I am Success, and I am prosperity. I am Svaha, I am Svadha, I am Reverence, and I am Fate, and, I am Memory.

verses.sanskrit: अथास्य पादौ जग्राह भीष्मश्चापि ननन्द तम्। मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय निषीदेत्यब्रवीत्तदा॥२१॥
verses.english: I live at the van and on the standards of victorious and virtuous kings, as well as in their homes, cities, and kingdoms.

verses.sanskrit: तमुवाचाथ गाङ्गेयो वृषभः सर्वधन्विनाम्। मां पृच्छ तात विश्रब्धं मा भैस्त्वं कुरुसत्तम॥२२॥
verses.english: I always live, O killer of Vala, with those foremost of men, the heroes longing for victory and unretrcating from battle.
